newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX says customer service is improving.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX says customer service is improving.

text.p: NYNEX Corp said on Monday it is tackling its problems with customer service and expects state regulators to consider the company's merger with Bell Atlantic Corp on a range of issues besides customer service.

"We're confident that our customers and regulators will examine service quality in the context of all the other benefits offered by the merger," said Ivan Seidenberg, NYNEX chairman and chief executive.
He said in a company release that customers should see significant improvements in service by the end of the year.
"We've put in place a program that is already starting to pay off, and I'm committed to clearing up these issues and having significant service improvement by the end of the year," Seidenberg said.

Seidenberg's comments are in response to reports that the New York State Public Service Commission may block the $20 billion merger of NYNEX and Bell Atlantic on the basis of the company's poor customer service record.
The company said there are five state regulatory bodies that have claimed authority to approve the merger: New York, Connecticut, Vermont, New Hampshire and Maine.
"We've been in constant contact with all our regulators," NYNEX spokesperson Bob Varettoni said. "But the service issue is primarily New York."
The company said it has started adding customer service employees and committed $1 billion in infrastructure improvements over the next five years.
NYNEX and Bell Atlantic said last week they aimed to close the merger pact by Jan. 1, 1997.
